justice: The wide, flat side lane provides a barrier-free physical surface that accommodates wheelchair users, supporting basic accessibility.
A complete lack of tactile paving discriminates against visually impaired pedestrians, significantly reducing spatial fairness.
The heavy allocation of spatial resources to multiple motor vehicle lanes compared to the single shared side path reflects inequitable road distribution.
safety: The raised median with vegetation effectively separates main vehicle traffic from vulnerable users, enhancing physical safety for cyclists and pedestrians.
A motor vehicle parked directly in the side path acts as an obstacle, forcing cyclists and wheelchair users to swerve and creating collision hazards.
The absence of traffic calming measures and marked crosswalks poses significant crossing risks for older adults and adolescents.
Tall streetlights are installed at regular intervals, providing necessary illumination for nighttime safety for all road users.
livability: The total absence of ground-floor commercial units and community facilities fails to support the daily needs of older adults and local residents.
The lack of active building frontages and pedestrian activity means there are no 'eyes on the street', severely reducing social surveillance for adolescents.
The environment is completely isolated from the distant residential buildings, drastically reducing street vitality and opportunities for social interaction.
sustainability: Extensive impermeable asphalt surfaces dominate the right-of-way, with no visible green stormwater infrastructure or infiltration facilities.
Linear planting of shrubs and young trees provides only basic green infrastructure, lacking the ecological benefits of a mature urban canopy.
The sprawling, vehicle-centric road design inherently encourages carbon-intensive driving over active transportation modes.
aesthetics: Consistent placement of streetlights and uniform, clear lane markings create a visually clean and orderly road rhythm.
Neatly trimmed shrub barriers along the median add a structured layer of greenery to the landscape.
The barren expanses, lack of architectural diversity, and presence of high-voltage power lines result in a monotonous and uninspiring visual experience.
comfort: Sparse, immature trees provide almost no shade, leading to poor thermal comfort for elderly pedestrians and cyclists during hot weather.
The complete lack of benches or resting facilities negatively impacts the physical comfort of older adults who require frequent breaks.
The smooth, well-maintained asphalt paving offers a comfortable and jolt-free physical surface for mobility aids and bicycles.
walkability: The paved side path offers continuous walking space without sudden drop-offs, accommodating basic pedestrian movement.
The lack of pedestrian-scale amenities, such as shade and seating, severely diminishes the feasibility and attractiveness of walking long distances.
Visual isolation and a lack of engaging street-level features make the walking experience tedious for all social groups.
bikeability: The physical separation created by the planted median provides an excellent safety buffer from high-speed motor vehicles for cyclists.
Obstructions such as the parked black car in the side lane force cyclists to brake or detour, significantly reducing cycling convenience.
Continuous and smooth asphalt paving ensures low rolling resistance, supporting physically efficient cycling.
